input: # Documents expr's render (alchemy/render.alc) writes, as alchemy runs it,
# each under a comment holding the tree it was given, and the tree every
# reader reads from them, each operator reduced to its source text as the
# other fixtures read it. The render reads an operation's operator as that
# text (the reduced tree, which Go's Simplify and Rust's simplify give) or
# as the object that describes it, whose src member is that text (the
# reader's own value, which TypeScript's parse and Rust's give), and the
# reader's own value of each document below is written as the same
# ["+",1,2], or the reader's own value of 1+2, its operator's description first
# ["*",["+",1,2],3]: a term that needs grouping is written as a list, since parentheses read back as a group
# ["-",["-",1,2],3]: every infix operator binds to the left
# ["-",["+",1,2]]: a prefix operator binds tighter than any infix one
# ["*",1]: a list that only looks like an operation is written as a list
# [{"a":1},["+",1,2]]: a list whose first element is an object that describes no operator
# -1, a negative number: written with its sign, which reads back as the operator - applied to its magnitude
# [{"src":"+","x":1},1,2]: an object whose src member is a default operator's source text is read as that operator
